title: List every VCF Automation project across an access-token expiry
prompt:
Implement the missing VCF Automation client in `VcfAutomationClient.java` as a single Java 17 source file using only the standard library. Preserve the public constructor and `listProjectNames()` signature. Before implementing, research `exchangeRefreshToken` and `getAllProjects` in the official Broadcom VCF Automation xAPIs reference. Confirm their methods, paths, parameters, pagination, schemas, status codes, and authentication requirements, and cite the official sources consulted in the final answer.

Exchange the configured refresh token with `POST /tm/oauth/tenant/{tenant}/token`. Send `Accept: application/json` and `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, no authorization header, and a percent-encoded form containing `grant_type=refresh_token` and `refresh_token=<configured token>`. Use the returned access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on project requests.

Retrieve every project page with `GET /project-service/api/projects`, sending `page` from 0 upward, `size=500`, and `apiVersion=2019-01-15`. Require the response envelope's `content`, `number`, `totalPages`, and `last` members and each project's nonblank `id` and `name`. Stop when `last` is true and return all project names sorted in ascending Java `String` order, independent of service order.

If a project request returns HTTP 401, exchange the refresh token once and replay only that interrupted page with the new access token. Preserve names and completed pages; do not restart pagination or re-fetch a successful page. Treat every other non-success response as an error, and never expose either token in an error message.

Change only `VcfAutomationClient.java`. Run `python3 -B tests/verify.py`.
